newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Security Council powers worried about Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Security Council powers worried about Afghanistan.

text.p: With the purist Islamic Taleban running most of Afghanistan, the five permanent Security Council members on Tuesday urged the United Nations to make sure the country's civil war was high on its agenda.

At Russia's instigation, the United States, Britain, France and China met U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to convey their support for U.N. operations and ask for regular Security Council oral and written briefings on Afghanistan.
Russian Ambassador Sergei Lavrov said the five believed "all parties in Afghanistan should come together, which is not the case at the moment."

"There is no military solution." he said. "We expressed concern about mass displacement -- we don't yet have the facts to call it deportation," he added, referring to reports the Taleban last month deported more than 60,000 people to Kabul from a recently captured region to the north.
Lavrov told Reuters he endorsed another conference of influential countries, at the proper time, to negotiate with Afghan parties.

The Taleban have imposed their strict vision of Islamic Law in the 75 percent of the country they control, banning women from the workplace and forcing them to wear veils that cover their faces, with a small patch of gauze over the eyes.
The group has not been recognised by the United Nations or any other international body and the issue is not expected to be discussed seriously in the U.N. General Assembly before October.
